title: Ky
description: Tiny and elegant HTTP client based on the Fetch API.

data.text: Ky is a small HTTP client built on the Fetch API with retries, timeouts, and hooks.

data.title: Ky request with retry

data.text: Ky is a small wrapper around the native `fetch` that adds a base URL, retries, timeouts, and `beforeRequest`/`afterResponse` hooks, while still returning a real `Response`. That means the API you already know from `fetch` keeps working, and it runs in the browser, in Node, and at the edge.

data.title: A configured ky client

data.text: Retrying a non-idempotent `POST` can create duplicate records, so ky defaults to retrying only `GET` and only on specific status codes. It also backs off between attempts. Configuring retries at the client level keeps that policy out of individual call sites.

data.title: Per-request retry override
Why not just use fetch
data.text: The honest answer is that ky is a thin layer: no `Response.json()` boilerplate, no manual `AbortController` timeout plumbing, and retries built in, at roughly a couple of kilobytes. If a project already has axios, adding ky is rarely worth it. Good answers name the size and the fact that it stays close to the platform.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Ky wraps Fetch with better defaults.
